raw_response:
**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been doing this for 30 years. I know this land and I know the seasons in Quzhou. My wheat-maize rotation takes up most of the farm — about 12 mu — and I plant cotton on the remaining roughly 5 mu on separate plots. The cotton is getting harder to manage since my son works in the city now, but I am not ready to give it up entirely. Cotton prices were decent last year.

For wheat, I plant after maize harvest in October. I use Jimai 22 — it does well here and I know how it behaves. I apply fertilizer generously at planting and then topdress at jointing. With well irrigation, I can give it four waterings: before winter sets in, at jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray twice for aphids and once for powdery mildew. I use rotary tillage to break up the compacted soil after maize.

For summer maize after wheat, I seed directly into the stubble — no-tillage saves me time and my back. I use Xianyu 335, a hybrid that has served me well. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate twice if it's dry. Less pest pressure than cotton.

Cotton I plant in April after spring tillage. Bt cotton means I spray less for bollworm but still need to manage aphids and whitefly — I plan seven applications total. Cotton needs potassium, so I put more in. Four irrigations minimum.
